notes: Stepper's own props are only children, modes, style, testID and accessibilityLabel; each stage's text, status and colour are Step props and modes, so rules about them carry no target here (the Step entry targets them). The package declares no mode collections for Stepper, but the evidence shows Stepper merges its modes into every Step (the Step's own win), so Step Status is recorded as an evidence-created mode. Evidence spans three checks: 5 October (0.1.78-3795b4c), 8 October (0.1.78-636f3f5, which fixed #195: list semantics, current step, status words, status setting the colour) and 13 October (0.1.78-c1fa197, installed; no designer-facing change recorded). The 5 October line that a complete status without the Step Status mode renders a check on purple is superseded by the 8 October check; only its second clause (upcoming steps stay purple unless set to inactive) is used. Guide problems: (1) the States description says the status sets the colour "so a check is always green", but the Sources note says an explicit Step Status mode overrides the colour, and the Don't "Put a check on purple" depends on that override; "always" holds only without an explicit Step Status mode. (2) The Stepper guide never says that upcoming stages need Step Status inactive (only the Step guide and this guide's evidence do); its States table shows Upcoming as a state without saying how to get it. (3) The Sources note says each stage is read with its title plus the status word; in the installed c1fa197 source, Step also reads a short supporting text (up to 80 characters, one line) and, with a StepLabel child, that child's title. The 13 October evidence says no designer-facing behaviour changed, so the guide and evidence were not updated for this. (4) Dark mode (#197) was last checked on 5 October; the Step evidence lists #197 as in Review on 10 October, so the Dark gap may be stale. The guide names no other component to use instead.

examples.purpose: KYC progress with a spoken name, upcoming stages set to inactive, and the next action as a separate Button.
examples.jsx:
<VStack modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Stepper accessibilityLabel="KYC progress" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
    <Step title="Verify PAN" supportingText="Match your PAN with your name" metaText="Done 2 Oct 2026" status="complete" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
    <Step title="Add bank account" supportingText="Link the account you’ll invest from" metaText="Started 5 Oct 2026" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
    <Step title="Add nominee" supportingText="Choose who receives your investments" metaText="Due by 12 Oct 2026" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Step Status': 'inactive' }} />
    <Step title="eSign" supportingText="Sign the form with an Aadhaar OTP" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Step Status': 'inactive' }} />
  </Stepper>
  <Button label="Continue" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</VStack>

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: Stepper clones every element child with index, its own modes merged into the child's (the child's win), and showLine (false on the last child). It is vertical only, not interactive, and owns no current step.
evidenceFacts.quote: It clones every element child with `index`, merged `modes` (the child's win), and `showLine` (false on the last child).

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: Merged into every Step child, whose own modes win; a Step Status set here colours every step the same.
evidenceFacts.quote: A Stepper-level `Step Status` colours every step the same.

evidenceFacts.name: Step Status
evidenceFacts.description: Colour comes from the Step Status mode on each Step: active (the default), inactive, complete, error or warning. Set on the Stepper, it colours every step the same.
evidenceFacts.quote: Colour comes from the `Step Status` mode on each Step: `active` (default), `inactive`, `complete`, `error`, `warning`.

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Names the list: on the web Stepper renders a ul named by accessibilityLabel, and each Step an li.
evidenceFacts.quote: Stepper renders a `ul` (named by `accessibilityLabel`) and each Step an `li`.

evidenceFacts.name: testID
evidenceFacts.description: Works on Stepper, Step and StepLabel.
evidenceFacts.quote: `testID` works on Stepper, Step, and StepLabel.
